talks.title: Your Agent Is Wasting Tokens and You Don't Know It

positions.claim: Caching the system prompt reduces the payload on every call after the first, since only a much reduced system prompt is sent subsequently.
Prompt caching is not specific to Strands Agents — it works across model providers.
You should not use the most expensive model for every task; agents should route across multiple models based on use case.
A cheap model can be used as the router that decides which model handles a given request.
Large tool results should be stored outside the context and summarized rather than re-sent to the LLM on every loop iteration.
Agents should always set a maximum iteration count on tool loops, because uncapped loops can run 10-20 times or become infinite.
Observability tooling should be run on tool calls before deploying an agent to production.
Resending full conversation history in multi-turn agents can consume hundreds to thousands of tokens per call.
Sliding-window history trimming costs you the beginning of the conversation, and summarizing the dropped history into context is the right mitigation.
Token waste in agents is largely an engineering-hygiene problem solvable with five well-known tactics rather than requiring model or architecture changes.
